# Nxeon creator promo

A 50-second sponsored segment for the Nxeon Creator Partner Program. Every product screen is rebuilt as motion graphics from the real portal recording, using the real layout, copy and prices. Each creator gets their own render: their code, partner URL, play address, game and language.

Built with [HyperFrames](https://hyperframes.heygen.com) (HTML → video, GSAP). There's no audio, so creators narrate over it and add their own music.

## Quick start

```bash
node tools/render-creators.mjs --list              # what would render (reads creators.csv)
node tools/render-creators.mjs --format 16x9       # final 1080p60 16:9 for every creator + language
node tools/render-creators.mjs                     # 16:9 and 9:16
node tools/creator-kit.mjs                         # HOW-TO-USE.txt + end-frame PNGs next to each creator's videos
```

The output goes to `renders/creators/<CODE>/nxeon-promo_<CODE>_<lang>_<16x9|9x16>.mp4`.

Renders run one at a time because the machine is CPU-only. A final 50 s video takes about 2–3 minutes. Add `--draft` for 30 fps previews, which take about 1 minute each.

## Adding or changing a creator

Edit `creators.csv`. Only `code`, `url`, `game` and `languages` are required:

| column | example | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | `ZEROSTER` | uppercase, up to 16 characters; the chip and fields auto-fit |
| `url` | `https://nxeon.cloud/partner/ZEROSTER` | shown without `https://` |
| `game` | `Valheim` | Minecraft, Minecraft Bedrock, Valheim, Rust, Project Zomboid, Palworld, Factorio, The Forest, Enshrouded, Terraria. Anything else falls back to Minecraft |
| `languages` | `en;es` | `en` English, `es` Spanish, `tr` Turkish, `hi` Hindi, `tl` Tagalog |
| `handle` | `ArmyOfZeus` | optional; shown as "with @handle" on the end card |
| `discountFirst` / `discountAfter` | `50` / `10` | optional; defaults 50 / 10 |
| `priceBefore` `priceAfter` `renewPrice` | `$4.99` `$2.49` `$7.18` | optional per-game price overrides (defaults are Minecraft 2 GB from the recording) |
| `upgradePrice` `upgradeRenew` `tier8Price` | `$4.05` `$12.94` `$23.02` | optional; the upgrade beat |

Render one creator with: `node tools/render-creators.mjs --only HOVEN` (add `--lang es` or `--format 9x16` to narrow it further).

The game swap changes only the game's name and cover, in the game pick, the order summary, the dashboard header and the end card. Settings, mods and the upgrade tiers stay Minecraft UI, and prices stay Minecraft's unless you override them in the CSV.

## Generic version

`node tools/render-creators.mjs --generic` also renders a version with **"USE MY CODE"** and an empty code chip. Creators who aren't batch-rendered can put the transparent code overlay on top of it.

## Transparent overlay kit

```bash
node tools/render-overlays.mjs                  # generic kit → renders/overlays/ (placeholder code YOURCODE)
node tools/render-overlays.mjs --only HOVEN     # that creator's code, language and URL → renders/creators/HOVEN/
```

ProRes 4444 `.mov` with alpha (1920×1080, 60 fps, first and last frames fully transparent):

| file | length | what |
|---|---|---|
| `nxeon-overlay_sting` | 2.5 s | NX mark slam → NXEON wordmark → tagline |
| `nxeon-overlay_code` | 6 s | "USE CODE {CODE}" chip, −50% badge, partner URL, bottom-left |
| `nxeon-overlay_endcard` | 6.5 s | logo, code chip, offer, URL, game chips; holds still for ~3.5 s |

They're designed for dark or busy footage: the wordmark and tagline are white, and the end card carries a dark scrim so the text stays readable. The end card is large (about 650 MB) because ProRes 4444 is lossless-ish; creators can transcode it to a smaller alpha format if they need to. The 9:16 overlays aren't built yet.

## Rendering a single video by hand

```bash
npx hyperframes render -f 60 -q high --variables '{"code":"HOVEN","game":"minecraft","lang":"es","url":"nxeon.cloud/partner/HOVEN"}' -o out.mp4
npx hyperframes render --composition compositions/vertical.html ...      # 9:16
npx hyperframes preview                                                   # live Studio preview with editable variables
```

All variables are declared at the top of `index.html` (`data-composition-variables`).

## Project layout

```
index.html                  16:9 composition (1920×1080, 50 s): clip windows + persistent layers
compositions/vertical.html  9:16 composition (1080×1920): same scenes + src/vertical.css
compositions/overlay-*.html transparent overlay compositions (sting, code lower-third, end card)
src/data.js                 beat timing table (NX.T), games + covers, overlay strings per language
src/lib.js                  shared components: labels, stepper + tab-rail spines, cursor, wipes, 9:16 mapping
src/main.js                 reads variables, mounts scenes, builds the one paused timeline
src/scenes/s01–s12.js       one file per beat (html + motion)
src/promo.css, vertical.css styles (vertical.css only re-positions panels for 9:16)
assets/                     fonts (Geist, Geist Mono, Noto Sans Devanagari), logo, covers, flags, icons, mod icons
creators.csv                the batch list
tools/                      render-creators.mjs (batch), render-overlays.mjs (alpha kit), creator-kit.mjs (notes + end frames)
BRIEF.md, STORYBOARD.md, frame.md   the brief, the beat plan, the design spec
```

## Changing things

- **Copy and translations:** `NX.STRINGS` in `src/data.js`. `[brackets]` mark the highlighted word. Only overlays are translated; the recreated portal UI stays English on purpose, matching what viewers will actually see. Have a native speaker skim each language before publishing.
- **Timing:** edit `NX.T` in `src/data.js`; scene exits are written relative to each beat's end. Then update the matching clip windows (`data-start` / `data-duration`) in `index.html` and `compositions/vertical.html`, and the root `data-duration` if the total changes.
- **Adding a game:** add a portrait cover to `assets/covers/` and an entry to `NX.GAMES` (`src/data.js`), then add its name to `GAMES` in `tools/render-creators.mjs`.
- **Adding a language:** add a block to `NX.STRINGS`, then add the code to `LANGS` in `tools/render-creators.mjs` and to the `lang` variable options in both HTML files. Scripts outside Latin and Devanagari need a font in `assets/fonts/` with an `@font-face` in both HTML files.
- **9:16 layout:** panel positions and zoom are in `src/vertical.css`. If you move a panel that has cursor clicks, update its entry in `NX.VMAP` (`src/lib.js`).

Always run `npx hyperframes check` after editing; it should report 0 errors.

## Notes and caveats

- **"Live in seconds"** is the client-confirmed claim. In the reference recording the deploy took about 11 minutes (the game download step), so the video shows the build compressed and puts no clock on screen.
- **Privacy:** no account email, server IP or account name from the recording is shown. The play address is built from the code (`<code>.play.nxeon.cloud`).
- **Disclosure:** the "SPONSORED" chip is on by default (`sponsoredTag` variable). Creators must still tick YouTube's paid-promotion box.
- **Fonts:** Geist and Geist Mono (OFL, from the `geist` npm package) and Noto Sans Devanagari (OFL), all bundled locally in `assets/fonts/`. Licences are next to them.
{
  "name": "nxeon-creator-promo",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.140 preview",
    "check": "npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.140 check",
    "render": "npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.140 render",
    "publish": "npx --yes hyperframes@0.8.140 publish"
  }
}

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- **node-2 sandbox** (optional, not required): `nxeon-fsn1` (178.63.94.114), tree at `/opt/nxeon-v2`, its own DB (`nxeon_v2`), `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` (stubs Proxmox provisioning + Stripe charges only — everything else is real code against a real, separate DB). Useful for large or highly experimental work in isolation; not part of the normal edit→stage→promote path above. Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at `STAGING_HOST` (or `:8080`, with the TLS caveat above) → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. Test changes on staging before promoting — always.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

 * only had 2), added on top of the untouched existing ladder.

 * per-family table + method):

 *     script only INSERTS new rows, it never updates an existing GamePlan.
 *   - Each new tier is sized off lib/game-player-recommend.ts's own fitted
 *     player→resource curve for that family (the same curve the live deploy
 *     wizard/custom-plan slider already uses), snapped to a "nice" RAM value.
 *   - A smaller ENTRY tier is added below the current floor wherever the
 *     curve says that's a real, runnable size for the game; where the
 *     existing floor is already the practical minimum (or the curve is a

 * per-database anyway) before adding each family's 4th tier, so staging
 * matches prod's catalogue shape everywhere.

So I'm weighing whether to add optional spec variables per tier to the template so each game shows accurate vCPU, disk, and player numbers, even though that touches several places like the order summary and dashboard resource displays.

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac
  WS="$BH_ROOT/wt/$NAME"
  ENVF="/etc/nxeon-build/wt/$NAME.env"
  DBNAME="wt_$(echo "$NAME" | tr '-' '_')"
  PORT=$(( 4100 + $(printf '%s' "$NAME" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1) % 800 ))
}

# Create the node-2 side once: dir, owner marker, throwaway DB, env file.
ensure_remote() {
  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
[ "\$(hostname)" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || { echo "not node-2" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p $(q "$WS") /etc/nxeon-build/wt; chmod 700 /etc/nxeon-build/wt
mk=$(q "$WS/.devhost-owner")
if [ -f "\$mk" ] && [ "\$(cat "\$mk")" != $(q "$TOP") ]; then
  echo "workspace $NAME belongs to \$(cat "\$mk") — set DEVHOST_NAME=<unique> for $TOP" >&2; exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' $(q "$TOP") > "\$mk"
. /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env
if [ ! -s $(q "$ENVF") ]; then
  sec=\$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | head -c 48)
  ( umask 077; cat > $(q "$ENVF") <<EOT
# devhost env for $NAME (node-2 only, throwaway). NEVER production values.
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://\$AGENT_PGUSER:\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD@127.0.0.1:5433/$DBNAME?connection_limit=10
AUTH_SECRET=\$sec
APP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT
PORT=$PORT
COOKIE_SECURE=false
NXEON_DEVHOST=1
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=5120
EOT
  )
fi
export PGPASSWORD="\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD"
if ! psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U "\$AGENT_PGUSER" -d postgres -tAc "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='$DBNAME'" | grep -q 1; then
  createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U "\$AGENT_PGUSER" $DBNAME && echo "created throwaway database $DBNAME (node-2 127.0.0.1:5433)"
fi
EOF
}

push_files() {
  # Source only: git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored files. node_modules, .next,
  # .git and every .env* stay where they are (rsync never deletes excluded files).
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  rsync -a --delete --compress --compress-choice=zstd -e "ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" \
    --exclude=/.git --exclude=/node_modules --exclude=/.next --exclude='/.next.*' \
    --exclude='/.env' --exclude='/.env.*' --include='.env.example' --exclude='.env*' \
    --exclude=/.devhost-owner --exclude=/.devhost-deps --exclude='/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo' \
    --filter=':- .gitignore' \
    "$TOP/" "$BUILD_HOST:$WS/"
}

# npm install + prisma generate when package-lock.json / schema changed (or forced).
deps() {
  local force="${1:-0}"
  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
cd $(q "$WS")
h=\$(cat package-lock.json prisma/schema.prisma 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
if [ "$force" = 1 ] || [ ! -d node_modules ] || [ "\$(cat .devhost-deps 2>/dev/null)" != "\$h" ]; then
  echo "devhost: installing deps on node-2 (npm install + prisma generate)..."
  $(q "$BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" agents --dir "$WS" --env "$ENVF" --unit "nxeon-dev-$NAME-deps" --max 1800 -- \
      bash -c 'npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3 && npx prisma generate 2>&1 | tail -1') </dev/null
  echo "\$h" > .devhost-deps
fi
EOF
}

prepare() { init_ws; ensure_remote; push_files; deps 0; }

REMOTE_UNIT=""
cleanup_remote_unit() {
  if [ -n "$REMOTE_UNIT" ]; then
    bh_ssh "systemctl stop $(q "$REMOTE_UNIT") 2>/dev/null; true" </dev/null || true
  fi
}

run_remote() {  # run_remote LOCK MAX CMD...
  local lock="$1" max="$2"; shift 2
  local args=(agents --dir "$WS" --env "$ENVF" --unit "nxeon-dev-$NAME-$$")
  [ "$lock" = 1 ] && args+=(--lock)
  [ -n "$max" ] && args+=(--max "$max")
  REMOTE_UNIT="nxeon-dev-$NAME-$$"
  trap cleanup_remote_unit EXIT
  trap 'exit 130' INT TERM HUP
  local rc=0
  bh_ssh "$(q "$BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" "${args[@]}" -- "$@")" </dev/null || rc=$?
  REMOTE_UNIT=""
  return $rc
}

cmd="${1:-help}"; shift || true
case "$cmd" in
  help|-h|--help) sed -n '2,33p' "$0" ;;

  sync)
    # All local branches + tags -> node-2 mirror refs/remotes/primary/* (pruned
    # within that namespace only). Release builds push their exact commit too.
    GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" git -C "$REPO" push -q --force --prune "$BUILD_HOST:$BH_MIRROR" \
      '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/primary/*' '+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*'
    say "mirror synced ($(git -C "$REPO" for-each-ref refs/heads | wc -l) branches)" ;;

  push) init_ws; ensure_remote; push_files; say "pushed $TOP -> node-2:$WS" ;;
  install) init_ws; ensure_remote; push_files; deps 1 ;;

  run)
    lock=0; max=""
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
      case "$1" in --lock) lock=1; shift ;; --max) max="$2"; shift 2 ;; --) shift; break ;; *) break ;; esac
    done
    [ $# -gt 0 ] || die "usage: devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD..."
    [ "$lock" = 1 ] && [ -z "$max" ] && max=1500   # keep the shared lock bounded (release builds wait max 30 min)
    prepare
    run_remote "$lock" "$max" "$@" ;;

  tsc)   prepare; run_remote 0 1800 npx tsc --noEmit "$@" ;;
  test)  prepare; if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then run_remote 1 1500 npx tsx --test "$@"; else run_remote 1 1500 bash -c 'npx tsx --test test/*.test.ts'; fi ;;
  build) prepare; run_remote 1 1500 npx next build "$@" ;;

  dev|bg)
    if [ "$cmd" = dev ]; then bname=dev; else bname="${1:?usage: devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...}"; shift; fi
    case "$bname" in *[!a-z0-9-]*) die "bad name $bname" ;; esac
    init_ws; port="$PORT"
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
      case "$1" in --port) port="$2"; shift 2 ;; --) shift; break ;; *) break ;; esac
    done
    if [ "$cmd" = dev ]; then set -- npx next dev -H 127.0.0.1 -p "$port"; fi
    [ $# -gt 0 ] || die "no command"
    ensure_remote; push_files; deps 0
    unit="nxeon-dev-$NAME-$bname"
    bh_ssh "systemctl stop $(q "$unit") 2>/dev/null; $(q "$BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" agents --bg --dir "$WS" --env "$ENVF" --unit "$unit" -- env PORT="$port" "$@")" </dev/null >/dev/null
    say "started $unit on node-2 (127.0.0.1:$port only). Logs: scripts/devhost logs $bname -f"
    say "reach it from the primary:  scripts/devhost tunnel $port   (then http://127.0.0.1:$port)"
    say "or test it ON node-2:        scripts/devhost run -- curl -s http://127.0.0.1:$port/"
    say "stop it when done:           scripts/devhost stop $bname" ;;

  stop)
    init_ws; which="${1:-all}"
    if [ "$which" = all ]; then
      bh_ssh "for u in \$(systemctl list-units --plain --no-legend 'nxeon-dev-$NAME-*' | awk '{print \$1}'); do systemctl stop \"\$u\"; echo \"stopped \$u\"; done" </dev/null
    else

#!/bin/bash
# Run a command on node-2 INSIDE the capped build slice. Runs ON node-2.
# Called by scripts/devhost and scripts/lib/buildhost.sh from the primary.
#
#   run-capped.sh agents|prod [options] -- CMD [ARGS...]
#     --dir DIR        working directory (default /)
#     --unit NAME      transient unit name (default nxeon-run-<pid>)
#     --bg             start as a background service (dev servers); prints the unit
#                      name and returns. Stop with: systemctl stop NAME
#     --max SEC        RuntimeMaxSec (default 7200 foreground, 14400 --bg)
#     --env FILE       extra KEY=VALUE environment file (root-only), e.g. a worktree's
#                      dev env. NEVER a production .env.
#     --lock           hold /run/lock/nxeon-build.lock (one heavy job on node-2 at a
#                      time — `next build`, full test suites, Playwright suites)
#
# Foreground commands run as a transient SERVICE with --pipe --wait so CPU/memory
# accounting is reported when they finish, and they never leave the slice.
# Every process gets nice 10, ionice best-effort 7 and oom_score_adj 1000 (agents)
# / 500 (release builds), so if node-2 ever runs out of memory the kernel kills
# build/dev processes, never a customer VM (qemu processes keep their default 0).
set -euo pipefail
SLICE_KIND="${1:-}"; shift || true
case "$SLICE_KIND" in
  agents) SLICE=nxeon-build-agents.slice ;;
  prod)   SLICE=nxeon-build-prod.slice ;;
  *) echo "usage: run-capped.sh agents|prod [--dir D] [--unit N] [--bg] [--max S] [--env F] [--lock] -- CMD..." >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
DIR=/; UNIT=""; BG=0; MAX=""; ENVF=""; LOCK=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dir) DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --unit) UNIT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --bg) BG=1; shift ;;
    --max) MAX="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --env) ENVF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --lock) LOCK=1; shift ;;
    --) shift; break ;;
    *) echo "unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "no command" >&2; exit 2; }
[ "$(hostname)" = nxeon-fsn1 ] || { echo "run-capped.sh must run on node-2 (nxeon-fsn1), not $(hostname)" >&2; exit 1; }
systemctl is-active -q "$SLICE" || systemctl start "$SLICE"
TOOL=/opt/nxeon-build
UNIT="${UNIT:-nxeon-run-$$}"
case "$UNIT" in *[!A-Za-z0-9_.@-]*) echo "bad unit name $UNIT" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
[ -n "$MAX" ] || { [ "$BG" = 1 ] && MAX=14400 || MAX=7200; }

# Inside the 10 GB cap the memcg OOM killer picks by oom_score_adj too, so an
# agent process (1000) always dies before a release build (500); both die
# before any customer VM (qemu keeps 0) if node-2 itself ever runs out.
[ "$SLICE_KIND" = prod ] && OOMADJ=500 || OOMADJ=1000
props=(--slice="$SLICE" -p Nice=10 -p IOSchedulingClass=best-effort -p IOSchedulingPriority=7
       -p OOMScoreAdjust="$OOMADJ" -p RuntimeMaxSec="$MAX" -p WorkingDirectory="$DIR"
       -p KillMode=control-group -p TimeoutStopSec=20
       -E HOME=/root -E PATH="$TOOL/node/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"
       -E LANG=C.UTF-8 -E NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 -E npm_config_cache=/tank/nxeon-build/npm-cache
       -E npm_config_update_notifier=false -E TMPDIR=/tank/nxeon-build/tmp)
[ -n "$ENVF" ] && props+=(-p EnvironmentFile="$ENVF")

if [ "$LOCK" = 1 ]; then
  exec 7>>/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock
  if ! flock -n 7; then
    echo "==> waiting for node-2's build lock (/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock; a release build or another heavy job is running)…" >&2
    flock -w "${BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_SEC:-1800}" 7 || { echo "timed out waiting for the build lock" >&2; exit 75; }
  fi
fi

if [ "$BG" = 1 ]; then
  systemctl reset-failed "$UNIT" 2>/dev/null || true
  systemd-run --quiet --unit="$UNIT" --collect "${props[@]}" -- "$@"
  echo "$UNIT"
  exit 0
fi
# --pipe: stdin/stdout/stderr are ours; --wait: exit status + resource summary.

content.thinking:
I notice the order summary template literally composes the game name twice plus the plan size, like "Minecraft — Minecraft — 2 GB" — it's just concatenating product name and plan name from the recording. I'll keep that template behavior intact rather than trying to fix the duplication.

I'm now deciding to parametrize the plan specs with numeric variables (cpu/disk/players for each of the 2/4/8 tiers) rather than string templates, defaulting to the current Minecraft values so existing tools keep working, with players=0 meaning the "recommended players" line gets omitted. I still need to figure out the live "supported games" count versus the full GAME_FAMILIES list, and check how the actual tier upgrade UI formats the player recommendation line.

Now I'm sketching the overall architecture: adding a PromoRender model in Prisma tied to ReferralPartner, and working out stale-render detection where a worker's claim endpoint sweeps for RUNNING renders that have been stuck past a timeout and resets them to QUEUED.

I'll also add a hard-stale check at claim time using a heartbeatAt field, requeuing RUNNING renders whose heartbeat is older than timeout+10 minutes. For the build lock, I'm thinking the worker should take the flock per render task (rather than once for the whole job) so release builds only wait as long as a single format takes rather than the entire multi-format render.

Now I'm sketching the structure for lib/promo.ts, splitting out pure logic (formatting, cache keys, validation, tier selection) into lib/promo-core.ts and a separate lib/promo-howto.ts so these can be unit tested without touching the DB, and I need to figure out how the client card component gets its list data since it can't import lib/promo directly.

For the API routes, I'm planning app/api/promo/route.ts for GET/POST and a file route with Range support similar to the kits route pattern. Rather than risk modifying the shared kits route, I'll extract the Range-handling logic into its own helper file and use it only in my new route to avoid touching existing code.

For access control, I want to mirror kitAccess: either the owning partner via currentUser, or billing-staff via realUser, since the handoff notes staff real-user access should always work regardless of impersonation restrictions on admins.

For the worker-facing API routes (claim, progress, file upload, done, fail), I'm authenticating via a secret header compared with timingSafeEqual against an environment variable, returning 404 if the feature is disabled when the env var is unset. I also need to check middleware.ts to make sure the worker routes aren't blocked by existing auth/CSRF/origin checks on POST requests.

creator-partner-terms.pdf`. Two lines in it are broader than the code: a blanket "40% for life"
(the real rate is each partner's own `commissionRatePct`, default 20 — true only if every creator
partner is set to 40) and "50% off … any service except domains" (hosting/email don't carry the
discount yet — see above).

**Creator media kits — sponsored-segment videos (2026-10-08).** Each creator can have their own
sponsored-segment cut (one video per language, an end-frame still, a `HOW-TO-USE.txt`), shown at the
top of their portal's **Media kit** tab as "Your sponsored segment", plus a **Generic English
version** every partner sees. Code: `lib/partner-kits.ts` (listing, grouping, guide parser, zip),
`lib/partner-kit-access.ts` (auth), `lib/partner-kit-urls.ts`, `components/nx/PartnerMediaKit.tsx`,
routes `app/api/creator-partner/kits/[code]/[file]/route.ts` (one file) and
`app/api/creator-partner/kits/[code]/route.ts` (the whole kit as a zip); test
`test/partner-kits.test.ts`.
- **Folder layout** (under `NXEON_PARTNER_FILES_DIR`, default `/opt/nxeon/partner-files/`, outside
  the repo/build — same dir as the PDFs above):
  ```
  partner-files/kits/<CODE>/      one folder per ReferralPartner.code, UPPERCASE, ^[A-Z0-9-]{2,20}$
  partner-files/kits/_generic/    shown to every partner
  ```
- **Naming convention** (what groups a video with its end frame and labels the language):
  `nxeon-promo_<CODE>_<lang>_16x9.mp4` + `nxeon-promo_<CODE>_<lang>_16x9_endframe.png` (the PNG is
  the player's poster and a download; optional) + one `HOW-TO-USE.txt`. Languages are labelled from
  the tag (`en` English, `tr` Turkish, `tl` Filipino (Tagalog), `es` Spanish, `hi` Hindi, others in
  `KIT_LANGUAGES`); English is listed first. The generic folder uses `GENERIC` as the code. Allowed
  extensions: mp4/webm/mov, png/jpg/webp, txt, pdf; anything else, dotfiles, symlinks and
  subfolders are ignored (never listed, never served). A file that matches no pattern is still
  offered under "Other files".
- **HOW-TO-USE.txt** is parsed (not dumped): title + `====` underline, then column-0 headings with
  indented bodies — "Your files" (`- name` list + optional prose), "What it is", "How to use it"
  (numbered steps), "Suggested narration (…)" (`0:00  text` lines; wrapped lines continue the
  previous one), "Description text" (shown in a box with a Copy button), "Questions: <email>".
  Unknown sections are still shown. The raw file stays downloadable. In the generic guide the
  placeholder `YOURCODE` is replaced with the viewing partner's real code on screen (the download
  is unchanged).
- **Publishing a creator's kit is a file copy, no deploy** (the page reads the folder on every load):
  ```
  install -d -o nxeon -g nxeon -m 0755 /opt/nxeon/partner-files/kits/<CODE>
  install -o nxeon -g nxeon -m 0644 <files…> /opt/nxeon/partner-files/kits/<CODE>/
  ```
  Replacing a file = copying over it. Removing the folder hides the block (the partner then sees
  only the generic version, with a line saying their own is on the way). A folder with no video
  shows nothing.
- **Auth** (`kitAccess`): signed out = 401; a signed-in partner gets only their OWN code's folder and
  `_generic`; billing-area staff (ADMIN, BILLING — the same gate as `/admin/partners/<id>`) get any
  folder; everyone else, any other code, and any name not in the folder listing = 404 (never 403, so
  the URL space isn't advertised). `currentUser()` follows impersonation, so an admin impersonating a
  partner sees exactly that partner's files. The file name must exactly match a whitelisted entry
  of the directory listing — no path is ever built from the URL alone (`..`, encoded separators and
  absolute paths are refused). Responses: correct content type, `inline` (player/preview) or
  `attachment` with `?download=1`, single HTTP Range (`bytes=a-b`, `a-`, `-n`; 416 past the end) so
  the in-page player can seek, `HEAD`, `private, no-store`, `nosniff`, `default-src 'none'; sandbox`.
  The zip is STORE-only (videos don't compress), streamed with an exact Content-Length (CRCs are
  computed first and cached per file size+mtime).
- **Admin**: `/admin/partners/<id>` has a read-only "Media kit files" card — the partner's folder
  (name, size, updated, Preview link, "Download all") and, collapsed, the generic folder.

Everything below this line is **history**, not reference. It is kept because the *reasons* recorded in
these entries are often the only surviving explanation for why a piece of code looks the way it does.
Where an entry contradicts Parts I–VI, **Parts I–VI win** — they were verified against the tree; these
were written at the time.

## How to read the change history

```

   3. "Session log — 2026-07-26/27"             the most recent waves
 Authoritative alternatives when an entry looks stale:

```

The gate now judges the wallet *after* today's debit. Hosting orders paid by PayPal, crypto or a local method now need a saved card or a wallet that covers a renewal. This change also adds a read-only gap report, a banner that is off by default, and a drafted email that nothing sends. ## Session log — 2026-07-26 into 2026-07-27 (the customer-readiness push)

Seven commits, newest first. This document was last verified at `4ea9790`; everything above it in this
table is what the current pass folded in.

| Commit | Subject | Verified state |
|---|---|---|

The extraction of `lib/renewal-charge.ts` was forced by a bundling failure (`Can't resolve 'fs'`) that `tsc` could not see |

Two of the three agents behind this commit were killed mid-task; what is recorded here is what was verified afterwards, not what was intended |

| `4ea9790` | Promo-basis proration, post-cutover TLS, 8 more migration defects | **Real.** `Server.termPromoPercent` makes the proration round trip net zero by construction; the TLS pass stopped being dead code; 4 rows backfilled from real billing records with 0 fallbacks |
| `fd71056` | Migration rehearsal fixes, proration symmetry, wallet floor, CI | **Real.** Nine engine defects, the `capMonths` asymmetry, the sub-Stripe-floor card leg, and the first CI workflow |

The through-line across all seven is the defect this codebase keeps producing in new places: **a second
definition of something that already had one.** A second renewal formula. A second promo basis. A
second place `lastAutoBackup` could be written. A second email-normalisation. The fix, every time, was
to delete the duplicate rather than to make the two agree.
- Badge: `components/nx/CyrusBadge.tsx` (`CyrusBadge`, `CyrusSeal`) — a ringed-monogram seal + small caps, token colours, `tone="onDark"` for dark islands. **Every** Cyrus surface renders the mark only through this file, so the Cyrus redesign can swap it in one place.
- Servers listed in the Cyrus install modal now need to be RUNNING (the engine installs onto the running server); stopped ones show "start it to install".

**B2 — updates, history, rollback.** `getModsOverview` adds `cyrus` to each Cyrus row (`lib/cyrus-mods/installed.ts`: installed vs current version, labels like `v2 · 1.1.0`, update available, version count, page slug) and sets `availableVersion` from the chain (so the update badge and the Updates count include it). The **Versions** dialog (`mods/CyrusVersions.tsx`, actions in `lib/actions-cyrus-installed.ts`) lists every finished version newest first with its release notes (the builder's own "what changed", else the change request), marks "On this server" / "Latest", offers **Update to latest** and **Roll back to this** (confirm step; one engine `update` job with `targetVersionId`; the replaced jar is backed up). "Latest" = the creator's restored head in Cyrus (`cyrus.headBuildId`) when set, else the newest success. Two versions with the same version string get a distinct package version (`1.1.0+<id6>`), so the engine's idempotency check can't skip a real switch.

**B3 — auto-generated pages.** `lib/cyrus-mods/doc.ts buildModDoc(chain)` (pure) → `CyrusModPage.doc`: name (Cyrus title, else plugin name), tagline, summary, how to use, limitations, commands, permissions, config, compatibility (Paper/Purpur + every MC version built for), versions + changelog, current version, source file list. `lib/cyrus-mods/pages.ts syncCyrusModPage(root)` creates the page when a chain's **first** version succeeds and regenerates it on every later one (hooked into `lib/modbuilder/store.ts syncBuild`, so both the API routes and the worker sweep trigger it; never fails a build). Older builds are backfilled when their creator opens the Cyrus Mods page. Slugs: kebab of the name, de-duplicated.
- Routes: portal `/dashboard/nxlabs/cyrus` (index: your mods + published ones, search) and `/dashboard/nxlabs/cyrus/<slug>`; public `/mods/cyrus` and `/mods/cyrus/<slug>` (`app/(marketing)/mods/cyrus/**`; the middleware keeps them out of the NXM rewrite and its anonymous cache header). NxLabs home gets a **Cyrus Mods** section and tab (`LabsTabs cyrus`) for gated viewers.
- Page: header (seal, title, badge, creator display name — never any part of an email — version, licence, forks, "forked from"), Overview / Versions / Community tabs, download source + jar per version, sha256, Build on this.
- **Open source**: every page offers the source. `/api/nxlabs/cyrus/<slug>/download?what=source|jar&build=<id>` (gated like the page, rate-limited 30/10 min) serves the jar from the store and the source zip from the build service — cached on the primary as `<jar dir>/<id>.source.zip` after the first fetch — repacked with `LICENSE` and `NXEON-CYRUS.md`. Licence: **MIT by default**, creator-selectable from MIT / Apache-2.0 / MPL-2.0 / GPL-3.0-only / BSD-3-Clause / Unlicense (`CYRUS_LICENSES`). MIT and Unlicense texts are reproduced in full; the others ship a copyright line + SPDX id + the canonical SPDX URL (owner decision whether to embed full texts).
- **Private by default.** Only the creator can publish (`setCyrusPageVisibility`, with a confirm that says exactly what publishing means) or make it private again. Admins can hide a whole page.

**B4 — community.** `CyrusModPost` threads (`parentId=null`) and comments, `kind` NOTE / BUG / FIX, `status` OPEN / RESOLVED, optional `buildId` (a version of this mod; a bug report must name one when there are several). Rules in `lib/cyrus-mods/community.ts` (pure, tested): resolve = thread author, creator, admin; delete = author (own), creator, admin (thread delete takes its replies + reports); hide/unhide = creator, admin; report = any signed-in viewer except the author, once per post (`CyrusModReport`), **auto-hidden at 3 reports** until reviewed. Rate limits are DB counts (hold across processes): 5 threads/hour, 30 comments/hour, 20 reports/day per user, 10 forks/hour. Posting needs a verified email. Every write is refused while an admin is impersonating (writes need the real signed-in account to be the effective one; reads show what the customer sees). Every action is audited (`cyrusmods.*`).
- **Build on this mod** (`forkCyrusMod`): the creator just opens their version in Cyrus. Anyone else (who has Cyrus access) gets their OWN copy of the chosen published version: a new succeeded `ModBuild` (jar copied, docs copied, title "<name> (fork)") + `CyrusFork{buildId, sourceBuildId, sourcePageId}`; their copy gets its own private page with "forked from". Change requests on the copy are sent to the build service with the ORIGINAL build as base (`serviceBuildId()` in `app/api/mod-builder/builds` POST, `/source`, `/source-zip`), because the service only knows the original. Forks of forks resolve to the original.

**Gating (must stay hidden until launch).** `lib/cyrus-mods/gate.ts`: allowed = Setting **`cyrus_mods_public_enabled`** (default `"false"`) OR a modbuilder preview account (`preview_access_emails_modbuilder` / `preview_access_emails`, default the owner). Outside the gate every route 404s (titles say "Page not found"), every action answers "Not found", downloads 404, the NxLabs section/tab are not rendered, pages are `noindex`, and nothing is in the sitemap. After launch: published pages are visible to everyone (indexable), private pages still only to their creator/admins; the sitemap lists `/mods/cyrus` + published pages (`lib/sitemap-sections.ts`). Building on a mod still requires Cyrus access (private preview). **To launch:** `/admin/cyrus-mods` → "Launch Cyrus mods publicly" (or set the Setting). **Schema (additive, `prisma db push`):** `ServerMod.targetVersionId String?`; new tables `CyrusModPage`, `CyrusModPost`, `CyrusModReport`, `CyrusFork` (FK-less ids). No existing column changes.

**Mod health.** Cyrus rows record `ServerMod.fileName` (the jar the engine placed), and `lib/mod-health.ts nameForms` now also tries the jar name without its version suffix (`Heal-1.1.0.jar` → `Heal`), so a Cyrus mod whose page title differs from its plugin name still gets a verdict.

**Known limits.** Cyrus mods are skipped by the auto-updater (no upstream; they change only when the owner picks a version). Installing someone else's published Cyrus mod straight onto your server is not offered (download the jar, or Build on it to get your own copy) — owner decision.

#!/bin/bash
# Provision / refresh the build host (node-2) FROM THE PRIMARY. Idempotent.
#
#   scripts/buildhost/provision.sh            # toolchain (if changed) + setup-node2.sh
#
# 1. Ships the primary's EXACT Node toolchain (/usr/bin/node + npm + corepack —
#    the same binaries nxeon-web runs on) to /opt/nxeon-build/node on node-2.
#    node-2's own /usr/bin/node (v24, used by the staging/sandbox/v2 copies
#    there) is NOT touched; builds put /opt/nxeon-build/node/bin first on PATH.
# 2. Copies scripts/buildhost/*.sh to /opt/nxeon-build/bin and runs
#    setup-node2.sh there (slices, datasets, mirror, throwaway Postgres).
# 3. Pushes all branches + tags into node-2's mirror (refs/remotes/primary/*).
set -euo pipefail
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo "run as root" >&2; exit 1; }
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=../lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/../lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

[ "$(bh_ssh hostname)" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || { echo "$BUILD_HOST is not $BUILD_HOST_NAME" >&2; exit 1; }
want="$(node -v) npm $(npm -v)"
have=$(bh_ssh "[ -x $BH_TOOL/node/bin/node ] && echo \"\$($BH_TOOL/node/bin/node -v) npm \$(PATH=$BH_TOOL/node/bin:\$PATH npm -v)\"" || true)
if [ "$want" != "$have" ]; then
  echo "==> Shipping Node toolchain ($want; node-2 had: ${have:-none})"
  tmpd=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$tmpd"' EXIT
  mkdir -p "$tmpd/node/bin" "$tmpd/node/lib/node_modules"
  cp -a "$(readlink -f "$(command -v node)")" "$tmpd/node/bin/node"
  cp -a /usr/lib/node_modules/npm /usr/lib/node_modules/corepack "$tmpd/node/lib/node_modules/"
  ln -s ../lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js "$tmpd/node/bin/npm"
  ln -s ../lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npx-cli.js "$tmpd/node/bin/npx"
  ln -s ../lib/node_modules/corepack/dist/corepack.js "$tmpd/node/bin/corepack"
  bh_ssh "mkdir -p $BH_TOOL && rm -rf $BH_TOOL/node.new"
  tar -C "$tmpd" -cf - node | bh_ssh "mkdir -p $BH_TOOL/node.new && tar -C $BH_TOOL/node.new --strip-components=1 -xf - && rm -rf $BH_TOOL/node.old && { [ -d $BH_TOOL/node ] && mv $BH_TOOL/node $BH_TOOL/node.old || true; } && mv $BH_TOOL/node.new $BH_TOOL/node && rm -rf $BH_TOOL/node.old"
fi
echo "==> Installing build-host scripts into $BH_TOOL/bin"
bh_ssh "mkdir -p $BH_TOOL/bin"
# shellcheck disable=SC2086
scp -q $BH_SSH_OPTS "$HERE"/setup-node2.sh "$HERE"/remote-build.sh "$HERE"/run-capped.sh "$HERE/../lib/seamless-release.sh" "$BUILD_HOST:$BH_TOOL/bin/"
bh_ssh "chmod 755 $BH_TOOL/bin/*.sh && $BH_TOOL/bin/setup-node2.sh"
echo "==> Syncing the git mirror"

#!/bin/bash
# Install / update the CREATOR PROMO render worker on node-2 FROM THE PRIMARY.
# Owner/root only. Idempotent. Nothing is started unless you pass --start.
#
#   scripts/buildhost/promo-render-install.sh [--ref REF] [--start]
#
#   1. node-2: system user `nxeon-render` (no login, no home), dirs
#        /opt/nxeon-render/releases/<sha>   worker + template (git archive of REF, default main)
#        /opt/nxeon-render/current          -> the release in use
#        /opt/nxeon-render/tools            hyperframes 0.8.140, static ffmpeg/ffprobe, chrome-headless-shell
#        /tank/nxeon-render/work            scratch for renders (on tank, not the VMs' rpool)
#        /etc/nxeon-render/promo-render.env secrets/env (0640 root:nxeon-render) — created once, never overwritten
#   2. systemd: nxeon-build-render.slice (child of nxeon-build.slice, so the
#      10 G / 6-CPU build cap covers it) + nxeon-promo-render.service (non-root,
#      nice 19, idle IO, CPUQuota 300 %, MemoryMax 6G, OOMScoreAdjust 900, network
#      only to loopback + the primary). Every render task takes node-2's build
#      lock (/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock), so it never competes with a release build.
#   3. --start: daemon-reload + enable --now (or restart, when it already runs).
#
# The worker never gets a database credential: it talks to the app's
# /api/promo/worker/* pull API with PROMO_WORKER_SECRET (same value in
# /opt/nxeon/.env on the primary). See docs/DOCUMENTATION.md "Creator promo videos".
set -euo pipefail
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo "run as root" >&2; exit 1; }
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=../lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/../lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"
REF=main; START=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in --ref) REF="$2"; shift 2 ;; --start) START=1; shift ;; *) echo "unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
done
PRIMARY_IP="${PRIMARY_IP:-51.79.162.96}"
HF_VERSION=0.8.140
CHROME_BUILD=152.0.7977.30   # what hyperframes $HF_VERSION pins (CHROME_VERSION in its dist)

[ "$(bh_ssh hostname)" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || { echo "$BUILD_HOST is not $BUILD_HOST_NAME" >&2; exit 1; }
SHA=$(git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --short=12 "$REF^{commit}")
echo "==> Promo render worker: $REF ($SHA) -> $BUILD_HOST_NAME"

echo "==> User, dirs, tools"
bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF
set -euo pipefail
id nxeon-render >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd --system --no-create-home --home-dir /nonexistent --shell /usr/sbin/nologin nxeon-render
install -d -m 0755 /opt/nxeon-render /opt/nxeon-render/releases /opt/nxeon-render/tools
install -d -o nxeon-render -g nxeon-render -m 0750 /tank/nxeon-render /tank/nxeon-render/work
install -d -m 0750 -g nxeon-render /etc/nxeon-render
cd /opt/nxeon-render/tools
if [ ! -x node_modules/hyperframes/bin/hyperframes.mjs ] || ! grep -q '"version": "$HF_VERSION"' node_modules/hyperframes/package.json; then
  cat > package.json <<'PKG'
{ "name": "nxeon-promo-render-tools", "private": true,
  "dependencies": { "hyperframes": "$HF_VERSION", "ffmpeg-static": "5.3.0", "ffprobe-static": "3.1.0", "yauzl": "3.2.0" } }
PKG
  PATH=$BH_TOOL/node/bin:\$PATH npm install --no-audit --no-fund --omit=dev
fi
mkdir -p bin
ln -sfn ../node_modules/ffmpeg-static/ffmpeg bin/ffmpeg
ln -sfn ../node_modules/ffprobe-static/bin/linux/x64/ffprobe bin/ffprobe
CH=/opt/nxeon-render/tools/chrome/chrome-headless-shell/linux-$CHROME_BUILD/chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell
if [ ! -x "\$CH" ]; then
  rm -rf /opt/nxeon-render/tools/chrome/chrome-headless-shell/linux-$CHROME_BUILD
  PATH=$BH_TOOL/node/bin:\$PATH node_modules/.bin/browsers install chrome-headless-shell@$CHROME_BUILD --path /opt/nxeon-render/tools/chrome
fi
"\$CH" --version
EOF

The agents slice is already using 4.75 of 7 GB, so adding a dev server and render process concurrently risks OOM. I'm thinking the render worker should run as its own transient unit under the parent build slice instead, isolating it from the other processes to mirror how production would handle it.

Since the parent slice caps at 10G and the OOM killer prioritizes by oom_score_adj, I need to be careful not to accidentally kill other agents' processes while testing. A safer sequence is to start the dev server in the agents slice as usual, then spin up the render worker in a separate sibling slice so its memory footprint stays isolated and easier to monitor.

I'm weighing capping my dev test to 3G memory with a 300% CPU quota and two workers, but adding my own ~2G footprint on top of the existing agents usage pushes close to the 7G ceiling — too risky given another agent is already at 3.5G. Running a production build via `devhost build` instead isn't much better since it also competes for the lock and uses similar memory during the 5-8 minute build, so I should check whether that other agent's workload is about to finish and free up headroom before proceeding.

I'll just start the dev server now and watch usage, since typical Next.js dev footprint is only 1-1.5G anyway; I'll also set a lower max-old-space-size (3072) to cap heap growth without being so tight it risks an OOM crash. For the render worker, I'll place it as a sibling slice under the build slice with its own 3G cap, so combined with the 7G agents ceiling it stays within the 10G parent limit even in the worst case — so I'll set the environment variables first.

## Environments — production, staging, and the .env contract

The code is byte-identical between environments. Every difference is an environment variable. That
is the entire isolation model, which is why one wrong value in `.env` is how staging would eat
production's IP pool.

| | Production | Staging |
|---|---|---|
| Tree | `/opt/nxeon` | `/opt/nxeon-staging` |
| Database | `nxeon` | `nxeon_staging` |
| Web service | `nxeon-web.service` :3000 | `nxeon-staging-web.service` :3001 |
| Worker | `nxeon-worker.service` | `nxeon-staging-worker.service` |
| Terminal backend | `nxeon-terminal.service` | `nxeon-terminal-staging.service` |
| Console proxy | `nxeon-console-proxy.service` | `nxeon-staging-console-proxy.service` |
| VM IP pool | `10.20.0.100–250` | `10.20.0.50–99` |
| SSH DNAT ports | `20000–29999` | `30000–30999` |

input.message:
## Creator Promo: report

Partners can now generate their own sponsored-segment video (their code, language and game) from the partner dashboard. Two real 1080p60 16:9 renders went all the way through the new pull API on node-2: claim, render, upload, done. The feature is off until `PROMO_WORKER_SECRET` is set. Nothing is merged or deployed, and no production DB, emails or permanent units were touched.

**Branch:** `feature/creator-promo` in `/tank/dev-worktrees/creator-promo`. It has two commits, local only: the post-commit hook did not push the branch to origin.
- `1bb5f6f115` adds the template at `video-templates/creator-promo/`. It is template 1.1.0: I added nine tier-spec variables (`tierCpu*`, `tierDisk*`, `tierPlayers*`), so a Valheim video shows Valheim's vCPU, disk and player numbers instead of Minecraft's. The defaults are the recording's values.
- `5decca225a` adds the integration:
  - `PromoRender` model.
  - `lib/promo-core.ts` (pure, shared by the app, the worker and the tests), `lib/promo.ts`, `lib/promo-worker.ts`, `lib/promo-howto.ts`, `lib/range-file.ts`, `lib/actions-promo.ts`.
  - The `app/api/promo/**` routes.
  - The partner card `components/nx/PartnerPromoVideos.tsx`, placed under the media kit as "Make your own version".
  - The admin batch form `components/admin/PromoBatchForm.tsx`, plus a "Generated promo videos" card on `/admin/partners/<id>`.
  - The worker `worker-render/promo-worker.mts` (runs with plain `node`, needs no app install) and `scripts/buildhost/promo-render-install.sh`.
  - Tests, docs and ROADMAP.

**How it works**
- **Video data comes only from the DB:** the partner code, the `/partner/<CODE>` link, the fixed 50 %/10 % discounts from `lib/partner-discount.ts`, and live prices and specs from the game's active monthly 2/4/8 GB `GamePlan` rows.
- **Games without those three tiers are hidden.** Terraria was hidden in the test for this reason.
- **The pull API matches your design:** `claim` / `progress` / `PUT file?offset=` / `done` / `fail`, authenticated by a secret header. Without the secret, every route returns 404.
- **Uploads go in chunks of at most 8 MB** because nginx caps request bodies at 20 MB and Next middleware at 10 MB.
- **The app writes HOW-TO-USE.txt itself.**
- **Each render task holds node-2's build lock**, so a render and a release build never run at the same time.
- **Retries:** one retry, then FAILED. A render that stays quiet for 10 minutes is requeued. When the worker restarts, it reclaims a render that has been quiet for 2 minutes. I tested this live and it worked.

**Measured render times** (16:9, 60 fps, quality high, 2 HyperFrames workers, non-root unit capped at CPU 300 % / 3 GB):
